settings.question: How much does wheel balancing cost in Calgary?
settings.answer: Wheel balancing at Prince Tires in SW Calgary is $20 per wheel, or $80 for all four — and the whole job takes about 20 minutes. That's the standalone rate for re-balancing tires already on your vehicle. If you're buying tires from us, balancing is included in the installation.

settings.question: What's the difference between balancing and alignment?
settings.answer: Balancing is about weight — making the tire and wheel spin evenly so there's no vibration. Alignment is about angles — how the wheels are aimed, which shows up as pulling to one side and uneven tread wear. They're separate jobs: Prince Tires handles balancing; we don't do alignments. If your symptom is a shake or buzz at speed, balancing is the fix you're looking for.

settings.question: How long does tire balancing take?
settings.answer: About 20 minutes for all four wheels. Book a time online and there's no waiting around — drop the vehicle at our SW Calgary shop, we balance the wheels, and you're back on the road the same day.

settings.question: How do I know my wheels need balancing?
settings.answer: The clearest sign is a vibration that shows up at highway speed — around 90 to 110 km/h — and smooths out when you slow down. You'll feel it in the steering wheel, the seat, or the floor. It often starts after a hard pothole hit, and Calgary's spring roads on 16th Ave or McKnight are good at knocking a wheel out of balance.

settings.question: Is balancing included with new tires?
settings.answer: Yes. Every tire we install at Prince Tires is balanced as part of the installation, so a new set starts off smooth. The $20-per-wheel rate is for re-balancing tires that are already mounted — usually after a pothole hit, or when a vibration shows up between seasons.

settings.question: How often should tires be balanced?
settings.answer: Tires are balanced every time they're mounted. After that, re-balance when you feel a vibration, after a hard pothole hit, or when you notice uneven wear. A lot of Calgary drivers have it checked at their seasonal tire change.

settings.question: Where can I get my tires balanced in Calgary?
settings.answer: Both Prince Tires shops balance wheels for $20 per wheel: 111 42 Ave SW, just off Macleod Trail, (403) 452-4283, and Unit 101, 3928 Edmonton Trail NE, (825) 395-4024. Booking online takes a couple of minutes, and it stays a request until we confirm the time.

settings.question: Do you offer road force balancing?
settings.answer: Yes, at our Edmonton Trail NE shop. Road force balancing presses a loaded roller against the tire while it spins, so it finds stiff spots and runout a standard balance can't see — it's the next step when a vibration is still there after a regular balance. It's $35 per wheel. See road force balancing for how it works and when it's worth it.

settings.heading: Tire Balancing Service in Calgary
settings.subheading: Steering wheel buzzing at highway speed? That's a wheel out of balance. Tire and wheel balancing at Prince Tires is $20 per wheel ($80 for all four) and takes about 20 minutes — same-day at our SW Calgary shop.
settings.pricing_intro: The wheel balance price at Prince Tires is simple: $20 per wheel, or $80 to balance all four — about 20 minutes for the full set. We spin each wheel-and-tire assembly on a computer balancer, find the heavy spots, and add small counterweights until it runs smooth. No more buzz in the steering wheel at 100 km/h on Deerfoot. Balancing is already included whenever we install a new set of tires; the $20-per-wheel rate is for re-balancing tires that are already on your vehicle.

settings.text: Balancing is a weight problem — making the assembly spin evenly around its centre. Alignment is an angle problem, and it shows up as pulling or as one shoulder wearing faster. They feel different and they are different jobs.

settings.lead: Counterweights go on the rim, not the tire
settings.text: The balancer spins the assembly, finds the heavy spot and reports how much weight to add and exactly where. Small clip-on or stick-on weights cancel it out.

settings.lead: Static and dynamic imbalance are different faults
settings.text: Static imbalance makes the wheel hop vertically. Dynamic imbalance makes it wobble side to side. A modern spin balancer measures both planes at once, which is why weights sometimes go on the inner and outer lip of the same rim.

settings.lead: It gets worse with speed, not distance
settings.text: An imbalance you cannot feel at 60 km/h can be obvious at 110. That is why the symptom shows up on Deerfoot or Stoney and disappears on side streets.

settings.heading: What balancing actually fixes
settings.intro:
A tire and wheel are never perfectly even. The rubber varies slightly in thickness, the wheel has a valve stem on one side, and the whole assembly weighs about 20 kg. At 100 km/h it is turning roughly 800 times a minute.

A heavy spot of even 20 grams, spun that fast, throws the wheel off its axis hundreds of times a second. That is the buzz you feel.
settings.outro: Balancing is included with every new set installed here. The $20 per wheel rate is for re-balancing tires already on the vehicle. Book balancing or call (403) 452-4283.

settings.lead: A buzz that arrives at highway speed and leaves again
settings.text: Comes in somewhere around 90 to 110 km/h and smooths out as you slow down. That speed-dependence is the signature of imbalance.
Felt mostly through the steering wheel usually points to a front wheel. Felt through the seat or floor usually points to a rear one.
A hard hit can throw a weight off the rim or bend the wheel itself. April and May on 16th Ave, McKnight and Glenmore are when this turns up.

settings.lead: It started after a seasonal changeover
settings.text: Tires that sat all summer can develop flat spots, and a set moved onto different rims needs balancing again on those rims.

settings.lead: Pulling to one side is NOT balance
settings.text: A steady pull, or a steering wheel that sits crooked, is an alignment symptom — a different service from this one, and not something balancing will fix.

settings.heading: How to tell balancing is what you need
settings.intro: Vibration has several possible causes and only some of them are balance. What separates them is where you feel it and when.
settings.outro: If the vibration is constant at every speed rather than arriving at highway speed, it is more likely a bent wheel or a tire fault than a weight problem.
